SMTO-CFG-0081 — SMTO couldn't pick Skills automatically for this request

GUID: c881c543-4c9b-55c6-9249-ea7210f891b5
Slug: capability-selection-degraded
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_selection

What happened

  • The automatic Skill picker couldn't finish, so this request is using all the Skills you already allow. Nothing extra was permitted, and the task carries on.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task continue; you don't need to do anything for this request. It still runs with only the Skills you allow; it may just have more tools on hand than it needs.
  2. If this keeps happening, open Settings › Setup › Model routing and find the Automatic capability selection row. That row shows which model picks Skills for each request; if it reads Configure destination or enable fallback, no model is set up for it.
  3. If no model is set up there, turn on Allow fallback to Main in that row, or choose Main as its Destination. The picker then has a working model to use, so SMTO stops falling back every time.
  4. If the model is set up but slow, raise Capability selection timeout under Limits and recovery on the same page. A picker that runs out of time also causes this fallback.

What success looks like

  • New requests show Capabilities selected in the task activity instead of Using permitted capabilities.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. You can keep working meanwhile; this fallback never gives the agent permission you haven't allowed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Initial automatic capability selection fell back (compiler_hint_missing, selector_interrupted, output_invalid or selector_unavailable) and recorded a degraded selection epoch equal to the accepted capability ceiling.

What this means

  • Initial automatic selection falls back after a recorded selection failure and records a degraded epoch limited to the already accepted capability ceiling. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Initial automatic selection falls back after a recorded selection failure and records a degraded epoch limited to the already accepted capability ceiling.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect degraded_reason_code and accepted ceiling; no extra capability or operation permission was granted.

How to fix it

  • Check the selection epoch's degraded_reason_code and the selector call in the Server log or model output inspector. If it recurs, fix the Automatic capability selection route (Helper or Main model availability, capability_selection_timeout_seconds); the fallback stays within the accepted ceiling and normal permission checks.
  • Continue with the existing permitted capabilities; inspect the selector failure if it recurs rather than migrating unrelated settings.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The task continues under the recorded permitted fallback and normal tool availability/permission checks.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
